title: Hanko
description: A vermillion seal that stamps: the shu-iro signature for approvals, authorship and things that are done.
usage: The seal is cast in shu-iro — the same vermillion reserved for the mark and the live center of controls — because a hanko is exactly that: a signature with weight. It stamps in when it arrives (scale, a breath of overshoot, an ink ring that fades) and re-stamps on click. Use it where a human means it: approvals, signed releases, the end of a document that is finished.
a11y: The approval itself is stated in words beside the seal ("Approved — Mara Sato, Nov 2") — the text carries the approval for every reader. The stamp-in is a transform only and is skipped under prefers-reduced-motion, where the seal simply sits, already pressed.
